scope: Proposition 3.5 (Plane law and quantitative local comparison) of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Free coherent pairs in expanding regular hexagons converge on cylinder events to a law µ∞. This law is invariant under lattice translations, lattice symmetries, global sign changes, and interchange of the colors. If the domain of a finite pair law µE0,η contains a ball of radius L and has no constraints in that ball, then its restriction to a concentric ball of radius r differs from that of µ∞ in total variation by at most C(r/L)α, for L ≫ r ≥ 1. The associated plane height increments exist and have the same spatial symmetries. Every finite feasible prescription of B pins together with W = +1 on finitely many connected paths has positive plane probability.
